newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sharehodler pushes beverage spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sharehodler pushes beverage spinoff.

text.p: A Quaker Oats Co. shareholder will propose the company separate its food business from its beverage business, which includes the embattled Snapple line, according to the proxy statement filed in advance of the company's annual meeting.
The proposal, to be introduced by Leland Chalmers, a holder of 50,732 common shares, calls for Quaker to split the businesses into two separate companies by the end of the year.
A proposal by Chalmers last year that the company retain an investment banking firm to analyse this issue received only 11 percent of shares voting, the proxy said.
Quaker Oats' board recommended unanimously against the separation proposal.
The Snapple business has been under fire as it has posted an operating loss since Quaker acquired it two years ago in a $1.8 billion transaction.
Quaker Oats will hold its annual meeting May 14 in Rosemont, Ill.
The proxy statement also said that Quaker Chief Executive William Smithburg's salary rose 2 percent to $872,506 in 1996, with no bonus for the last two years.
Smithburg also exercised 79,312 options with realised value of $1.7 million, the proxy said.
